q-424.name: Question 1
q-424.worked_solution:
We start by using the power of quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3y}{{x}^{2}})}^{3} & = \\ \frac{(3y)^{3}}{{({x}^{2})}^{3}} & \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power of product rule in the numerator and the power rule in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(3y)^{3}}{{({x}^{2})}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{{3}^{3}{y}^{3}}{{x}^{2\cdot 3}} & = \\ \frac{27{y}^{3}}{{x}^{6}} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-424.html:
Question 1
?

(3yx2)3=

a
27y2x4
b
27y3x6
c
27y3x4
d
9y2x3
e
9y3x6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We start by using the power of quotient rule: (3yx2)3=(3y)3(x2)3

Then, we apply the power of product rule in the numerator and the power rule in the denominator: (3y)3(x2)3=33y3x2⋅3=27y3x6

q-2648.name: Question 2
q-2648.worked_solution:
First, we substitute for $x$ and $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}xy & =(\frac{81{a}^{8}}{{b}^{2}{c}^{3}})\cdot (\frac{{b}^{7}{c}^{11}}{9{a}^{4}}) \\  & =\frac{81{a}^{8}{b}^{7}{c}^{11}}{9{a}^{4}{b}^{2}{c}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we separate the fraction, group the three variables separately, and apply the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{81{a}^{8}{b}^{7}{c}^{11}}{9{a}^{4}{b}^{2}{c}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{81}{9}\cdot \frac{{a}^{8}}{{a}^{4}}\cdot \frac{{b}^{7}}{{b}^{2}}\cdot \frac{{c}^{11}}{{c}^{3}} & = \\ \frac{81}{9}\cdot {a}^{(8-4)}\cdot {b}^{(7-2)}\cdot {c}^{(11-3)} & = \\ 9{a}^{4}{b}^{5}{c}^{8} & \end{aligned}
$$

q-22308.name: Question 3
q-22308.worked_solution:
We start by using the product rule in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{2}\cdot {y}^{13}}{{y}^{12}} & ={y}^{n} \\ \frac{{y}^{2+13}}{{y}^{12}} & ={y}^{n} \\ \frac{{y}^{15}}{{y}^{12}} & ={y}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}^{15}}{{y}^{12}} & ={y}^{n} \\ {y}^{15+(-12)} & ={y}^{n} \\ {y}^{3} & ={y}^{n}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since both sides of the equation share the same base ($y$), we can equate the exponents:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{3} & ={y}^{n} \\ 3 & =n\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $n=3.$
